entry: Two repositories: "Octave already exists as a separate repo, so we just need to figure out how to communicate to the clients building those apps." Two products, one product owner each: "let's have one product owner for each because these are going to be two separate products launched independently." Every Octave app is native: "I think we should do the clients all natively for all the platforms." Built side by side: "in the Octave repo we're handling the development of those applications in tandem consecutively so that we're not waiting for each one to be built." A design language of Octave's own: "Given that these are all going to be written for different platforms, we should have a very well-codified design language." jellyscale owns what each reason means and the action it suggests; Octave owns the words. jellyscale ships a specific, tested Octave Web release in its image, and both are GPL-3.0-or-later as the owner would like ("I think the answer to all your questions is yes."); Octave's side of the licence is Octave's owner's. jellyscale's contract is the source of truth for what the server offers; each change to it reaches Octave as an issue labelled from:jellyscale, and Octave's requests come as issues labelled from:fluster, triaged by jellyscale's product owner. What jellyscale needs from Octave is asked on Octave's issue board, never planned as jellyscale's own task. Re-recorded on 2026-11-28 from the records named in `replaces`, which the tag `pre-rebuild` keeps. Quoted words are the owner's; the rest is the lead's record of 2026-11-27.
